title: rs-metadata validation report
description: The output contract of `rs-metadata validate --format json`. This is a stable interface: institutional tooling may consume it instead of scraping CI logs. Every renderer (human-readable text, GitHub annotations) is generated from this model, so the report is always a complete account of what the validator did.
$comment: Versioned with the tool that produces it: pin on the major component of tool.version. Additive changes bump the minor version; consumers should ignore unknown fields rather than fail.

status.description: Overall outcome. `passed-with-warnings` means no errors were found but recommendations went unmet; whether that fails a build is a policy decision made by `--fail-on`, not by the report.

generatedAt.description: UTC timestamp of the run, in ISO 8601. Omitted when SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH requests reproducible output.

version.description: The rs-metadata release that produced this report. The report format is versioned with the tool: pin on this major version.

profile.description: Which profile the anchor record was validated against, and which upstream vocabulary version that profile builds on.

root.description: The repository directory that was scanned, relative to the invocation or absolute.

sources.description: Every metadata source considered, including ones that were looked for and not found. Recording absent sources makes the report self-explanatory: a reader can tell the difference between 'no problems with pyproject.toml' and 'there is no pyproject.toml'.

checks.description: Number of comparison and profile checks evaluated, including those that passed silently.

diagnostics.description: All findings, ordered by severity and then by source and property. Errors and warnings are not split into separate arrays: consumers filter on `severity`, which keeps a single ordering and a single shape.

id.description: Stable adapter identifier, usable as a filter key.

file.description: Repository-relative path. For a source with status `absent`, the conventional path that was looked for.

formatVersion.description: Version of the source format as declared by the file itself, where the format declares one.

role.description: `anchor` is codemeta.json, the record everything else is compared against. `required` sources must be present. `optional` sources are auto-detected and skipped when absent.

status.description: `parsed` means the file was read and mapped. `absent` means it was looked for and not found. `unparsable` means it exists but could not be read, in which case a diagnostic explains why.

MappingRef.description: Which crosswalk was used to relate this source to CodeMeta, and where that crosswalk comes from. Recorded so a reader can tell an upstream CodeMeta mapping apart from one rs-metadata introduced.

origin.description: `codemeta-upstream` for mappings taken from the CodeMeta crosswalk tables; `rs-metadata` for mappings this project defines where no adequate upstream mapping exists; `mixed` when a mapping extends an upstream table.

source.description: URL of the upstream crosswalk, where one exists.

Location.description: Where in a file a finding applies. Line and column are 1-based and are resolved from the original file text, so annotations land on the offending line rather than on line 1.

path.description: Dotted or bracketed path to the value inside the source document, in the notation native to that format.

value.description: The observed value, rendered for display. Long values may be truncated.

code.description: Stable, descriptive diagnostic identifier. Codes are namespaced by the layer that produced them and never change meaning within a major version, so they are safe to use in filters, suppressions, and documentation links.

message.description: A complete sentence naming the affected metadata and stating what is wrong with it. Never generic.

property.description: The CodeMeta property the finding concerns, where one applies.

anchor.description: For consistency findings: the value in codemeta.json.

source.description: For consistency findings: the value in the other metadata file.

strategy.description: The comparison strategy that produced a consistency finding, which explains what counted as equivalent.

rule.description: The comparison rule applied: values must be equal, the source must be a subset of the anchor, or the two must merely overlap.

suggestion.description: Concrete remediation. Present whenever the validator knows what a correct value would look like.

docs.description: Link to the documentation for this diagnostic code.
